title: A few bioelectrically induced lens cells recruit host cells to build a normal-sized lens

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A few bioelectrically induced lens cells recruit host cells to build a normal-sized lens

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: When an ectopic lens is induced in tail tissue by bioelectric modulation, misexpressing the ion channel in only a small subset of the needed cells suffices: these cells recruit unmodified host cells to reach the critical mass for a normal-sized lens, so downstream modules such as size control are activated without micromanagement.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Navigation: an invariant between morphological, behavioral, and other spaces

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: For example, when an ectopic lens (in tail tissue) is induced by bioelectric modulation, it is sufficient to misexpress the channel only in a small subset of the needed cells: once their organ-level goal is specified, these cells will secondarily recruit other (un-modified) host cells as needed to achieve the critical mass needed to produce a normal-sized lens.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Navigation: an invariant between morphological, behavioral, and other spaces”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos with ion channel misexpression in tail tissue

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-19: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.61

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Lineage contribution and organ size operationalize the core finding. Published evidence can address the phenomenon, but distinguishing recruitment from differential survival or proliferation requires richer cell-level data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use lineage labels to estimate the modified and unmodified contributions to each ectopic lens and test whether sparsely modified founders recruit host cells while lens size approaches the normal distribution.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Normal size does not by itself identify an active recruitment mechanism.

Cell-resolved lineage images and injection-dose records may not be openly deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.87
data adequacy: 0.38
data existence: 0.48
discriminating power: 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Ectopic tail lens tissue after voltage perturbation, and a lineage label on the injected cells, are in an open paper with incidence counts. That paper's sections argue the labeled cells themselves took on eye identity, and it does not publish the host-cell fraction or a size-versus-clone curve the recruitment wording needs. Existing images can constrain the claim; they do not carry the cell-contribution table that would settle it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In mosaic channel misexpression with a lineage label, measure the fraction of unlabeled host cells inside ectopic tail lenses and plot lens diameter against the number of channel-positive cells. A normal-sized lens built mostly from unlabeled cells, after only a few labeled cells expressed the channel, would support recruitment; lenses composed only of the labeled clone, or size scaling with clone size, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A minority of injected cells forming eye tissue is a different measurement from those cells recruiting neighbors.

The published lineage result reports ectopic tissue as label-positive and does not tabulate an unlabeled host fraction.

Normal lens diameter is not plotted against the number of channel-expressing cells.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.76
analysis feasibility: 0.36
data existence: 0.42
data adequacy: 0.32
discriminating power: 0.5
